taskDescription: Arrange the steps of paracetamol hepatotoxicity in the correct order, from therapeutic metabolism to liver injury.
paragraphs: At therapeutic doses, about 90 percent of paracetamol is safely glucuronidated or sulphated and excreted.
About 5 to 10 percent is oxidised by CYP2E1 to the reactive electrophile NAPQI.
Glutathione conjugates NAPQI immediately, and the product is excreted as a mercapturic acid.
After an overdose, sulphation saturates and more paracetamol is shunted through CYP2E1, producing excess NAPQI.
Glutathione is consumed faster than it is made and falls below about 30 percent of normal.
Free NAPQI binds covalently to hepatocyte proteins, mitochondria fail, and centrilobular necrosis follows in zone 3.

overallFeedback.feedback: The sequence shows why paracetamol is safe at normal doses but lethal in overdose: once conjugation pathways saturate and glutathione is depleted, NAPQI attacks hepatocyte proteins. Zone-3 necrosis reflects high CYP2E1 concentration and low oxygen in the centrilobular region, and N-acetylcysteine works by replenishing glutathione before this threshold is crossed.
